newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio's Banerj sale still on hold, await Senate vote.
newsitem.headline: Rio's Banerj sale still on hold, await Senate vote.

text.p: The privatization auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj remains on hold as the bank's sale still hinges on Senate approval of a deal resolving the bank's debts, Rio state officials said.
The Senate's Economic Affairs Committee is due to vote on the matter Thursday.
But it is unclear whether the deal will be approved by the full upper house in time to allow Rio state to hold the auction before Friday.

Under the debt deal awaiting Senate approval, Rio state would assume Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts, which would be covered by a 3.09 billion reais loan from Caixa Economica Federal (CEF).

The state hopes to sell the bank as soon as the Senate approved the loan. The Banerj auction has been rescheduled for Thursday after two postponements, but officials said the sale could be delayed again until Friday.
Four banks -- Bradesco, Banco Itau, BCN and Cia de Investimentos Latino-Americana, owned by an unidentified foreign bank and represented by local Banco Pactual -- signed up for the auction.
Press reports on Thursday said that Banco Itau is not sure whether it will bid at the auction. Itau president Roberto Setubal was quoted as saying that Banerj's payroll-related debts are a concern.
Banerj, the first of Brazil's state banks due to be privatized, is slated to be sold off with a minimum price of 310 million reais in a closed-envelope auction.
